title: Lateral fanout stitch notes
content:
Goal:
- Quick exploratory scratchpad to understand how lateral fanout (1 -> N parallel subrequests) plus staggered warmup affects tail latency under small bursts (50-200 qps).
- Focus: SLO impact on p95/p99 and whether stitching responses increases variance at p99 under KV-cache cold vs warm conditions.

Hypothesis:
- Lateral fanout increases observed p99 by adding per-branch scheduling jitter and more opportunities for stragglers; staggered warmup (offset starts) should reduce cluster-wide peak but may increase individual request variance.

Setup (local cluster emulate):
- Topology: frontend proxy -> fanout router -> 3 identical model workers (vram-optimized) -> stitcher aggregator.
- Model: distilled-llama-like, 2.7B, seq_len 512, quantized FP16 path in runtime.
- Hardware: 3x rtx-6000 simulated (emulated latencies via p99 injector).
- Workload generator: custom replay harness (go), poisson arrivals with small bursts; payload sizes small (100 tokens avg).

Experiments run (short names):
1) baseline-single: no fanout, single worker (control).
2) fanout-sync: fanout to 3 identical branches, all started same time, aggregator waits for majority? (mode: earliest-2/3).
3) fanout-stagger: same as fanout-sync but branches have stagger start offsets (20ms, 50ms, 120ms) to emulate staggered warmup and priming.
4) fanout-no-priming: cold-KV caches on all branches (restart between runs).

Common load shape: 30s ramp to steady qps, 60s window at target qps, 30s cool down. Targets: 50, 100, 180 qps. Each run repeated 4x.

Important knobs recorded:
- batch_timeout_ms=8/16/32 (ran 16ms mostly)
- continuous_batching enabled
- kvcache priming enabled/disabled
- stitch_mode earliest-k (k=2) vs wait-all

Representative raw aggregated numbers (median of 4 runs, p50/p95/p99 in ms):
- baseline-single @100 qps: p50=28, p95=62, p99=98
- fanout-sync @100 qps: p50=36, p95=84, p99=165
- fanout-stagger @100 qps: p50=34, p95=76, p99=138
- fanout-no-priming @100 qps: p50=42, p95=110, p99=240

At 180 qps (closer to system saturation):
- baseline-single: p50=45, p95=140, p99=300
- fanout-sync: p50=58, p95=198, p99=520
- fanout-stagger: p50=54, p95=172, p99=410
- fanout-no-priming: p50=74, p95=260, p99=780

Observed patterns / notes:
- Fanout adds a consistent headroom penalty: p50 increases (extra routing + merge) and p95/p99 increase nonlinearly.
- Staggered starts helped reduce absolute p99 compared to sync (138ms vs 165ms @100 qps). Intuition: staggered branches avoid synchronized queue buildups and allow earliest-2 to finish earlier more often.
- Cold KV cache (no priming) dominates tail: p99 skyrockets; even at 50 qps, fanout-no-priming p99 ~ 300ms. Priming is critical for stitched requests.
- Under saturation (180 qps) tail amplification is multiplicative: any small variance per branch becomes larger at aggregator due to max/earliest-k semantics.
- batch_timeout tuning: raising from 8->32ms reduced p99 slightly for fanout-sync runs (fewer tiny batches, better GPU utilization) but increased p50 due to batching delay; tradeoff visible.

Quick ASCII micro-chart (p99 @100 qps):
baseline-single: 98  |*************
fanout-sync    : 165 |***********************
fanout-stagger : 138 |*******************
fanout-no-prim : 240 |*******************************

Per-branch telemetry (qualitative):
- Branch A occasionally saw kernel preemption at 70-90ms window (restarts on sim host).
- Branch C had higher GC pauses (python shim) when priming on cold runs.
- Aggregator overhead ~4-6ms median, but 25-40ms p99 when merging many partials.

Conclusions / advice (early):
- If using lateral fanout with earliest-k aggregation: enforce KV-cache priming and stagger branch warmup on rollout to avoid synchronized tail spikes.
- Consider earliest-1 when cost allows (reduce variance), or add per-branch SLAs that trigger branch-level circuit breakers on high latency.
- Tune batch_timeout to workload: small tokens benefit from slightly larger timeout to smooth batches, but watch p50 increase.
- Instrument per-branch queuing and expose sampling traces (need 1% end-to-end tracing on production).

Open questions / next runs:
- Test earliest-1 vs earliest-2 cost/quality tradeoff with same model variant (measure quality delta).
- Replace simulated kernel-preemption with real multi-tenant GPU noise to measure realistic straggler distribution.
- Explore adaptive stagger schedules: ramp offsets based on recent branch latency percentiles.
- Try aggregator heuristics: weighted-earliest (prefer branch with warm cache) or speculative cancellation.

Quick TODOs:
- [ ] Add 95/99 tracing span id correlation in harness (Samir)
- [ ] Run multi-day stability (12h) to check priming decay patterns (Maya)
- [ ] Prototype weighted-earliest aggregator (POC branch in PR 834)

Notes-to-self: keep these runs reproducible: save docker image tag, harness seed, and the per-run kernel-injector profile. Drop raw histogram dumps into /tmp/fanout-runs/YYYYMMDD if re-run.

-- J.P.
summary: Scratchpad for microbench exploring lateral fanout + staggered warmup effects on tail latency. Includes setup, runs, raw numbers, quick conclusions and next steps.
